landmarks.what: verify.toml persists each undisposed out-of-scope survivor (key, file:line, op, ambiguous) for close-out to re-classify
closeout_ack records upserted by item with a required reason, plus the phase/deferred/survivor item-id grammar
/dross-milestone completion arm runs --check first and walks each unresolved item one per turn (resolve / ack with reason) before opening the PR
collects unverified, not-done, unabsorbed-deferred and undisposed-survivor items with ack ids and clearing commands; collector errors become blocking lines
dross milestone ack <item> --reason records a closeout_ack for a currently-unresolved or already-acked item; unverified phases refused
milestone complete refuses with the full close-out report before any fetch/push; --force-unverified drops only the unverified kind; applied acks reach the PR body
milestone complete --check prints the close-out report with acks and stale acks, exits non-zero while blocking, never fetches, pushes or writes
partitions acks into applied and stale against produced items; Blocking counts unacked items plus collector errors; deterministic report render
not-done kind reuses phase.Done and contains the id before any stat; only ErrNotExist reads as unscaffolded

findings.text: undisposedSurvivors (internal/verify/verify.go:1093) treats every lifecycle value other than accepted/routed as undisposed, including in-diff and the empty unstamped state; in-diff cannot occur on out-of-scope rows per classifyOne, and the catch-all records rather than drops, so it fails towards noise
TestClassifyMarksOnlyWithheldAcceptancesAmbiguous pins that the flag means a withheld acceptance, not merely a repeated key, so a regression to stamping raw Identify ambiguity would be caught

test_contract names TestRoundTrip for the no-acks case (a toml with no acks loads a nil Closeout and re-saves without a closeout_ack key), but that check is in the separate TestNoAcksStaysAbsent in internal/milestone/milestone_test.go; the guarantee is still tested

FormatAckItem (internal/milestone/milestone.go) renders any non-deferred Kind as Kind:Payload without checking it, so a hand-built AckItem with an unknown kind formats silently; the result is unreachable from ParseAckItem output, and a later ParseAckItem call would reject it
parseIndex rejects leading zeros and '+' signs, so one deferred item cannot be written under two different ids; the extra rejection cases in the table test cover this

The description said to move existing §8 close-out prose into the partial to stay under 15000 B; instead the diff shortens the chore-PR and board-card sentences in place, and the partial contains only new walk text. By hand count milestone.md lands only a few dozen bytes under the budget; TestPromptByteBudget is what actually enforces it.

TestMilestonePromptCompletionArmChecksFirst reads the base prompt (milestoneBasePrompt), so the partial's own AskUserQuestion cannot skew the order check; the separate inlining check in the walk test covers the expanded prompt.

TestCloseoutCollectorErrorsAreBlockingLines makes spec.toml and survivors.toml malformed in the same root. routedSurvivors also calls deferred.Collect, so the bad spec alone already makes the survivor kind error. If closeoutSurvivorItems stopped reporting a survivors.toml load error, this test could still pass. Test survivors.toml in its own root with valid specs.

milestone_closeout.go:303: the routed-survivor clear hint reads "`dross survivor accept` survivor K". That cannot be run as written: accept takes <file>:<line> plus --op and --reason, not a key. The keyed-survivor hint in the survivor kind gives full arguments; this one should too, using the file:line and op parsed from the entry text.

boardsync.Disposed (existing code, internal/boardsync/disposition.go:47) ignores survivors.toml load errors. The deferred kind then lists the routed survivor, which is the safe direction, and the survivor kind reports the load error itself.
The narratedIgnore entry for `dross milestone ack` in cmd/dross/main_test.go is temporary. It is commented, and the hygiene check is expected to force its removal once t-5 registers the command.

TestCloseoutClearingCommands never checks how many survivor items come back. If the survivor kind returned nothing, the switch loop over ckKind(r.Items, closeoutSurvivor) would assert nothing and still pass. Assert that survivor:K, survivor:A and survivor:g.go:7:neg are all present.

closeoutNotDoneItems (internal/cmd/milestone_closeout.go:242) re-implements phase.IsDone instead of calling phase.Done/DirExists. It also stats phase.Dir(root, id) directly, skipping the ContainID escape guard that DirExists applies, so a phases entry like '../x' is stat'd outside phases/. Two definitions of done can drift apart.
closeoutNotDoneItems treats any os.Stat error, not just ErrNotExist, as 'no phase directory — unscaffolded roadmap entry'. A permission error still lists the phase, but the detail line is wrong.
If absorbedIDs fails for one target, closeoutDeferredItems stops there (milestone_closeout.go:322). Items for later targets are not listed, but the kind still carries a blocking error line.

closeoutKinds is declared but not used yet, presumably for t-5's rendering. narratedIgnore's temporary 'dross milestone ack' entry is guarded by the existing hygiene check, so it cannot outlive t-5's registration.
The unverified collector loads the milestone record a second time through milestoneUnverifiedPhases. This is harmless.

internal/cmd/milestone_ack.go checkAckable: the phase:<slug> refusal path never mentions r.Errors, unlike the non-phase path. If a collector failed, a phase that is in the milestone but has no unresolved item gets the message 'phase X is done — nothing to acknowledge', which may not be true. The refusal itself is still correct. It is low-risk in practice because the unverified collector only fails on a milestone load, and that load already succeeded earlier in the command.

A phase:<slug> that is already acknowledged is accepted before the unverified check runs. A phase acked while it was not done can therefore be re-acked after it becomes unverified. This is harmless: unverified items carry no ack id, so the ack never clears them, which still matches the locked force_unverified decision.
TestMilestoneAckRefusesEmptyReason also covers a missing --reason flag. The blank-reason check runs before FindRoot and before any read of the milestone file, so the toml cannot be touched.

The refusal message embeds renderCloseout output, which tells the user to re-run `dross milestone complete --check` when a collector fails. The milestone complete command has no --check flag yet (presumably a sibling task's job), so until it lands that hint names a command that does not exist.

milestoneCloseoutGate now runs before the [remote].url/.provider check in milestone.go. A project with no remote and unresolved items now gets the close-out refusal instead of the missing-remote error. The ordering is harmless and keeps refusals from moving any ref.
The c-10 finalize test calls loadCloseout first to confirm the fixture has unresolved items, so its 'finalize ignores close-out' check is not vacuous.

milestoneCloseoutCheck (internal/cmd/milestone.go) duplicates the load + force-unverified filtering in milestoneCloseoutGate (internal/cmd/milestone_verify_gate.go:97-104); a shared helper would keep the preview and the gate from drifting apart

the README roadmap checkbox ticked here also covers the /dross-review partial-value-set and swallowed-error reporting, which this task does not deliver; the task description asks for the tick, so this is recorded only

renderCloseout only iterates closeoutKinds, and closeoutKindRank falls back to len(closeoutKinds), so an Open item or Error with a kind outside the four constants would count in Blocking() but never be printed. No value reaches that path today: all four collectors use the constants in milestone_closeout.go:25-32.
In TestLoadCloseoutEmpty, the 'empty phases' case relies on ckRoot(t) saving a nil Phases slice rather than an explicit `phases = []`. Both load as empty, so the c-8 contract is still exercised.
loadCloseout stats and loads the milestone toml a second time after milestoneCloseout already loaded it. This is harmless but redundant I/O.

phase.Done/DirExists use the literal ContainID path with no legacy NN-slug fallback, while the old code went through phase.Dir (which falls back to the stripped slug). A legacy id like 01-auth whose directory is phases/auth now reads not-done and its detail says unscaffolded. This matches the shared doneness reader the task asked to reuse, but it is a behaviour change for close-out.

TestCloseoutNotDoneRefusesAnEscapingID cannot see a stat that happens outside the tree directly. It relies on the planted complete record at .dross/x, which would mark the phase done if anything outside were read. That is enough for the contract.
TestCloseoutNotDoneNamesOtherStatErrors depends on POSIX ENOTDIR behaviour when phases/ is a plain file. That is fine on the platforms the repo targets.
milestone_closeout.go:248 discards the boardsync.Disposed error (`ok, _ :=`) with no comment. That line predates this diff, so it is not a finding against this task, but it is worth a follow-up.
